subject: humanoid robot
title: A Robot Ran 100 Meters in 8.86 Seconds, Then Caught Fire

scenes.text: A robot beat Usain Bolt's 100 meter time. The finish didn't go well.
One year earlier, the same robot needed 21 and a half seconds.
In August 2026 in Beijing, the humanoid robot Tiangong Ultra ran a semifinal in 8.86 seconds. Bolt's record is 9.58.
That's more than twice as fast in a single year.
Its brakes? A thick mat past the finish line. It slammed in, collapsed, and a small fire broke out in its chest.
So yes, a robot beat Bolt. Bolt just never caught fire.

description:
A humanoid robot ran 100 metres faster than Usain Bolt's 9.58-second world record, then crashed into the mat that stops it. By the end of the games the humanoid 100 m record had been lowered again.
At the second World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing in August 2026, Tiangong Ultra (Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center) ran 9.39 seconds in a heat and 8.86 seconds in its semifinal, Reuters reported. At the first games a year earlier it won in 21.50 seconds. After the 8.86 run it struck a thick mat beyond the line, collapsed, and a small fire appeared in its torso. It is not an official world record: World Athletics records are for human athletes.
How long until robots race people for real?
first_comment: 21.50 seconds in 2025, 8.86 in 2026. Would you race it over 100 meters, or over a marathon?
